stem: Which of the following is contraindicated for day surgery ?
expl: Ileostomy reversal creates a bowel anastomosis — the patient needs admission to watch for ileus, leak and return of bowel function. The other operations can be day cases.

why.A: Elective lap chole is a classic day case.
why.D: Inguinal hernia repair is a classic day case.

stem: All of the following are social factors for day surgery criteria EXCEPT?
expl: Social criteria = responsible adult for 24 h, phone access, living reasonably close to the hospital, adequate understanding/education. "Access to a public area" is not a criterion.

stem: A patient is being discharged from the day surgery unit, you need to ensure all EXCEPT?

opts.t: Discharge summary with medical assistance overnight if needed
Appropriate Analgesia with written instructions given to the patient
Follow up in the emergency department for optimal postoperative outcome

expl: Day-surgery discharge needs a discharge summary, analgesia with written instructions, a contact for problems and clinic follow-up. Routine "follow-up in the ER" is not part of it.

stem: Which of the following surgeries requires in-hospital admission and cannot be performed as day surgery?
expl: Carotid endarterectomy needs inpatient monitoring (stroke, neck hematoma compressing the airway, BP instability, cranial nerve injury). Varicose veins, hemorrhoidectomy and partial thyroidectomy can be day cases.

why.D: Can be day case in selected patients.

stem: A patient is being discharged after a simple hemorrhoidectomy from the day surgery unit. What do you need to ensure before finalizing the discharge of the patient?

opts.t: Assessment by IM to ensure that the patient is medically fit
Sign-over verbally to the resident on-call at night in case the patient comes to the ER
Appropriate analgesia with written instructions given to the patient
A follow up in the ER for optimal post op outcome

expl: The key discharge requirement is adequate analgesia plus written instructions; a medically fit day-case patient doesn't need an IM review, night sign-over or routine ER follow-up.

why.A: Not needed for a fit day-case patient.
why.D: The ER is not a follow-up clinic.

stem: patient came to the hospital for open hernia repair as day surgery. Which of the following services do you need to assess the patient preoperatively?
expl: Every day-surgery patient is assessed by anesthesia beforehand (fitness for anesthesia and same-day discharge).

why.A: Only if a blood disorder exists.

stem: A 40 Year-old obese male was booked for a day surgery, anesthetic review preopertively assesed him as (low to intermediate risk),which of the following is the most likely cause?
expl: BMI 30–40 = mild systemic disease (ASA II) → low-to-intermediate risk; that is why he was rated so. Age 40 isn't a risk factor by itself.

why.D: Age 40 is not a significant risk factor.

stem: You're a medical student joining the surgical team in the operating room for the day , which of the following listed procedures could be considered as a day surgery?
expl: Source key: total mastectomy (can be done as a short-stay/day procedure in selected patients). Total thyroidectomy (hypocalcemia, hematoma), carotid endarterectomy and ileostomy reversal need admission.

stem: Which one of the following is a social factor for day surgery criteria?
srcNote: + B (Day Surgery) The question was cancelled.
expl: The question was cancelled in the exam because both A and B are social criteria (phone access and the area the patient lives in). A is shown as the answer here; B is equally correct.

why.B: Also correct — distance from the hospital (why the question was cancelled).
why.C: Education is also mentioned in the notes ("adequate understanding").

stem: A 33-year old woman admitted as gallstones for day case laparoscopic cholecystectomy. After surgery the patient was transferred to the ward. Which of the following is needed to be assessed during the post-operative?
expl: After a lap chole the first thing to assess on the ward is cardio-respiratory status (airway, breathing, circulation after anesthesia). Port-site hernia, infection and wound problems appear later.
